rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 2 (ki 0.4, all else as R1) scored 38.47, essentially identical to R1 at 38.61. Every trial in both races still ended off_track with 0 finishes. max_error stayed at 0.0607 to 0.0615 on every track, and each trial logged exactly one line_loss_event. Adding integral action changed nothing measurable, so the constant-bias hypothesis (H3) is rejected. Lowering kp and widening the footprint (iteration 1) also barely moved max_error. Across all three iterations, max_error is pinned just above the 0.06 m off-track limit, whatever the gains. The one consistent event is a single line loss per trial, followed by drift off the line.

Hypothesis. The sensor array is too narrow for the bends. The sensors span x = -0.04 to +0.04 m, plus footprint, so the tape leaves the array when the robot's lateral error or heading error is about 0.02 to 0.03 m. The line is then lost, and last_direction with throttle 0.35 cannot recover before the robot reaches 0.06 m. A wider span (x = ±0.07 m) should keep the tape under at least one sensor through the same bends and so avoid the line loss. Lateral error should then stay below 0.06 m.

Change. I widened the sensor span to x = -0.07, -0.035, 0, 0.035, 0.07 m, keeping five sensors, y = 0.05 m and the 16 mm footprint. The weights stay at -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, so the signal range is unchanged. I kept kp 2.0, kd 0.15, ki 0.4 (neutral in iteration 2, so it is harmless and keeps the test to one variable), base_speed 1.4 and line_loss last_direction. This is a single-variable geometry test. Speed and line_loss are held back until line loss is resolved.

Expected result. line_loss_events falls toward 0, max_error drops below 0.06, and progress rises well above 0.14. If line loss persists with the wider array, the next test is line_loss = search_left or search_right, and then sensor y placement.

Measurements wanted: max_error and rms_error per track, line_loss_events, progress, completion, steering_oscillation and completion_time. These show whether the span, rather than the gains, is the driver.
